title: Data poisoning as a bilevel problem
caption: The poisoner picks the poisoned set that maximizes damage *after* the defender's inner training loop runs on clean plus poisoned data. The untargeted form maximizes test loss; the targeted form instead minimizes loss on one chosen example, and backdoors hide inside either.

symbols.name: poisoned set
symbols.meaning: the attacker-chosen training examples or updates

symbols.name: clean data
symbols.meaning: the defender's honest training set

symbols.name: test distribution
symbols.meaning: the data the untargeted attack degrades

symbols.name: trained model
symbols.meaning: the model produced by training on the union

symbols.name: loss
symbols.meaning: the objective being maximized outside and minimized inside

symbols.name: trained parameters
symbols.meaning: the inner loop's result: the defender's optimum

title: Extraction break-even price
caption: Query-based extraction is worthwhile to the attacker only while the total bill for the query set stays below the cost of training the model itself. In the chapter's worked case, \$5M of training against 100M extraction queries puts the break-even at \$0.05 per query; pricing at or above that makes the full set cost about what training did.

symbols.name: query count
symbols.meaning: number of API calls the extraction attack needs

symbols.name: per-query price
symbols.meaning: what the attacker pays per call

symbols.name: training cost
symbols.meaning: the defender's cost to produce the model from scratch

symbols.name: break-even price
symbols.meaning: per-query price at which extraction costs exactly match training

title: Membership-inference ceiling under DP
caption: For a pure epsilon-DP release, no membership test, however clever, can push the true-positive rate above this ceiling at a given false-positive rate. At epsilon = 1 the bound bends near FPR 0.27: past that point the curve flattens and extra attack sophistication buys nothing.

symbols.name: true-positive rate
symbols.meaning: fraction of members the attack correctly flags

symbols.name: false-positive rate
symbols.meaning: fraction of non-members wrongly flagged

symbols.name: privacy budget
symbols.meaning: the DP bound on output-distribution change per protected unit

title: Robust aggregation traffic multiplier
caption: A gather-based coordinate-wise median receives every peer's gradient: $(N-1)M$ bytes per worker. Ring AllReduce moves about $2(N-1)M/N$. The ratio is $N/2$, so at $N=64$ robust aggregation costs roughly 32 times the per-worker gradient traffic of the ring, landing in the CommunicationTime term of the Fleet Law.

symbols.name: data-parallel degree
symbols.meaning: number of workers in the synchronous training job

symbols.name: gradient payload
symbols.meaning: bytes of one worker's gradient per step

symbols.name: gather traffic
symbols.meaning: per-worker bytes received by all-gather median aggregation

symbols.name: ring traffic
symbols.meaning: per-worker bytes moved by ring AllReduce

title: Approximate differential privacy
caption: For adjacent datasets $D$ and $D'$ differing only in the protected unit, and every measurable output set $S$, the release's probability of landing in $S$ can grow by at most the factor $e^\epsilon$ plus additive slack $\delta$. Pure DP sets $\delta=0$; Gaussian mechanisms need the slack because their tails have unbounded likelihood ratios.

symbols.name: mechanism
symbols.meaning: the randomized algorithm producing the release

symbols.name: dataset
symbols.meaning: the data the mechanism runs on

symbols.name: adjacent dataset
symbols.meaning: differs from $D$ in exactly one protected contribution

symbols.name: output set
symbols.meaning: any measurable collection of possible releases

symbols.name: privacy budget
symbols.meaning: multiplicative bound on output-probability ratios

symbols.name: additive slack
symbols.meaning: additive term in the bound, typically below $1/n$

title: Basic composition of privacy loss
caption: Ten models each released at epsilon = 1 on the same population compose to a basic bound of epsilon = 10, not epsilon = 1. The budget belongs to the history of data-dependent releases about the same protected population; mechanism-specific accountants tighten this sum.

symbols.name: composed budget
symbols.meaning: cumulative privacy bound across $k$ releases

symbols.name: per-release budget
symbols.meaning: the bound certified for release $i$

symbols.name: composed slack
symbols.meaning: additive slacks also accumulate

symbols.name: release count
symbols.meaning: number of data-dependent releases about the population

title: Laplace mechanism
caption: Pure-DP noise whose scale is the $\ell_1$ sensitivity divided by the privacy budget. In the salary-mean example the scale lands near \$200K at $\epsilon=1$, giving about a \$200 expected error on the mean of 1,000 employees and about \$2,000 on a 100-person group: small groups pay the largest relative cost.

symbols.name: private output
symbols.meaning: the released, noise-added query result

symbols.name: true query
symbols.meaning: the unperturbed aggregate

symbols.name: l1 sensitivity
symbols.meaning: maximum output change when one protected unit changes

symbols.name: privacy budget
symbols.meaning: smaller epsilon means more noise

symbols.name: noise scale
symbols.meaning: Laplace scale parameter $\Delta_1 f/\epsilon$

title: Gaussian mechanism calibration
caption: A classic sufficient bound for one application of the Gaussian mechanism with $0<\epsilon<1$. At $\Delta_2 f=1$, $\epsilon=0.5$, $\delta=10^{-5}$ the minimum sigma is about 9.7. This calibrates a single release; DP-SGD composes thousands of steps and needs a sampled-Gaussian accountant instead.

symbols.name: noise std dev
symbols.meaning: standard deviation of the added Gaussian noise per coordinate

symbols.name: l2 sensitivity
symbols.meaning: maximum $\ell_2$ change in output per protected unit

symbols.name: privacy budget
symbols.meaning: multiplicative bound on output-probability ratios

symbols.name: additive slack
symbols.meaning: tail-probability slack in the approximate-DP bound

title: Moments accountant composition
caption: The privacy loss random variable is the log-likelihood ratio between adjacent datasets. The moments accountant accumulates its exponential moments across steps and applies the tail bound once at the end, certifying tighter budgets than summing per-step bounds. In the Abadi experiment it reports epsilon 1.26 at 100 epochs and 2.55 at 400 where advanced composition reports 9.34 and 24.22.

symbols.name: privacy loss
symbols.meaning: log ratio of output probabilities on adjacent datasets

symbols.name: observed output
symbols.meaning: the realized release used in the ratio

symbols.name: log moment
symbols.meaning: exponential moment of the privacy loss at order lambda

symbols.name: moment order
symbols.meaning: the order being optimized over

symbols.name: step count
symbols.meaning: number of composed mechanism applications

symbols.name: additive slack
symbols.meaning: target tail probability for the composed bound

title: RDP composition and conversion
caption: Rényi DP bounds the alpha-divergence between output distributions on adjacent datasets, and per-step bounds add across composition. Converting the composed RDP guarantee back to $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP adds the slack term and optimizes over the order alpha. Subsampled mechanisms need a tested accountant; the leading-order shortcut does not certify a run.

symbols.name: RDP budget
symbols.meaning: the Rényi-divergence bound at order alpha

symbols.name: Renyi order
symbols.meaning: divergence order, greater than 1, optimized at conversion

symbols.name: additive slack
symbols.meaning: target slack in the converted DP guarantee

symbols.name: Renyi divergence
symbols.meaning: the divergence measure bounded by epsilon_RDP

title: Output-contract information budget
caption: Rounding a probability from 6 to 2 decimals removes about 3.32 bits per dropped decimal digit per class; returning only the top K of N classes keeps the fraction K/N of distribution entries. Both raise the query cost of a fixed-fidelity surrogate without constituting a privacy guarantee.

symbols.name: decimals dropped
symbols.meaning: reduction in decimal precision per probability

symbols.name: top-k
symbols.meaning: number of classes whose scores are returned

symbols.name: class count
symbols.meaning: total classes in the output distribution
